analysis.evidence: יָלַד means “fathered” here. Each of the four peoples listed after it is introduced by אֶת, identifying Mizraim as their ancestor.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וּ means “and.” The proper name מִצְרַיִם is the subject of the masculine singular verb יָלַד.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 68104:1, 66578:5, 66578:9, 66578:13.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks לוּדִים as the first direct object of יָלַד ‘fathered,’ whose subject is מִצְרַיִם. Each subsequent name is introduced by וְאֶת.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add the gentilic noun לוּדִי with its sense in Mizraim’s genealogy.
draft.definition: A Ludite, a member of the people called the Ludim.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:13 lists the Ludim first among the peoples fathered by Mizraim. The parallel genealogy in 1 Chronicles 1:11 gives the same sequence.

analysis.evidence: Mizraim is the subject of יָלַד, “fathered.” The object marker אֶת introduces לוּדִים, and the repeated וְאֶת introduces the Anamim, Lehabim, and Naphtuhim alongside them. The plural thus names a people among Mizraim’s descendants.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew gentilic noun, masculine plural absolute. The ending ־ִים marks the plural. The preceding אֶת is a separate word.
analysis.sense: A member of the people traced to Mizraim in the genealogy.

evidence.note: The Anamim are among the peoples Mizraim fathered.
The genealogy repeats the name in the same position among Mizraim's descendants.

article.name: עֲנָמִים
article.summary: The Anamim are a people descended from Mizraim. Both genealogies list them between the Ludim and the Lehabim.

draft.change: Add a name entry for the Anamim. Leave the root unassigned because neither genealogy establishes a derivation.
draft.definition: Anamim, a people descended from Mizraim.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:13 lists the Anamim among Mizraim's descendants. The parallel genealogy in 1 Chronicles 1:11 gives the same sequence.

analysis.evidence: Mizraim is the subject of יָלַד, “fathered.” The repeated object marker וְאֶת introduces עֲנָמִים between לוּדִים and לְהָבִים, identifying the Anamim as one of the peoples descended from Mizraim. The verse gives no etymology for the name.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew gentilic noun, masculine plural absolute. The ending ־ִים marks the plural. The word has no prefix or pronominal suffix.
analysis.sense: The people listed among the descendants of Mizraim.

analysis.evidence: The repeated object marker וְאֶת introduces לְהָבִים between עֲנָמִים and נַפְתֻּחִים. All three name peoples whom מִצְרַיִם is said to have fathered (יָלַד).
analysis.morphology: Gentilic noun, masculine plural absolute. The initial לְ belongs to the name.
analysis.sense: A people listed among the descendants of Mizraim.

draft.change: Add a standalone gentilic noun under its attested plural lemma. Use נפתח as its consonantal filing key. Its etymology is unknown, and neither genealogy supports the supplied root נפש.
draft.definition: The Naphtuhim are a people whom the genealogy traces to Mizraim.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:13 and 1 Chronicles 1:11 both name the Naphtuhim immediately after the Lehabim among Mizraim’s descendants.

analysis.evidence: In Genesis 10:13, מִצְרַיִם is the subject of יָלַד, “fathered.” The repeated object marker אֶת introduces each people in the list, with נַפְתֻּחִים fourth, immediately after לְהָבִים.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew gentilic noun, masculine plural absolute. The ending ־ִים marks the plural. The preceding וְאֶת is a separate word.
analysis.sense: the people called the Naphtuhim, counted among Mizraim’s descendants
